captured_on: Apple M1 Max, macOS Darwin 25.5, Node 25.9.0
notes: Budgets are PERMISSIVE — they catch order-of-magnitude regressions (e.g. eager parse5 load on the init path), not single-digit-ms variance.
GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runners run roughly 1.5-2x slower than this M1 baseline; budgets bake in that headroom.
If a budget here ever feels too tight in practice, raise it deliberately and record why in the corresponding scenario block — don't quietly relax.

cli-version-cold-start.description: `spectastic --version` — pure CLI startup; nothing beyond commander loaded
cli-version-cold-start.rationale: Node startup + ESM import of the entrypoint + commander. Regression past 150ms means something heavy was loaded eagerly; investigate the import graph.

init-help-cold-start.description: `spectastic init --help` — init module path; parse5 MUST stay lazy here
init-help-cold-start.rationale: If this grows toward validate's cost, init has accidentally started importing parse5 or schema's heavy deps. The I-019 lazy-import fix lives here; this scenario is its regression guard.

validate-single-cold-start.description: `spectastic validate <one-spec>` — first-doc cost including parse5 + all rules
validate-single-cold-start.rationale: Cold path: Node + commander + parse5 + every rule's module + parse one doc + run all rules once. The validate path's perf floor. RAISED 250 -> 350 on 2026-07-30: three legitimate additions to this exact cold path cumulatively tipped it past the old 250 cap on CI runners — spec 068's scanQuantifiedNfr/readQuantifiedNfrFloor (validate now reads spectastic.json + runs the quantified-NFR scan), then the commander 12->15 and parse5 7->8 major bumps (both marginally heavier module loads). CI observed p50 252 / p95 256. Deliberate raise per this file's own policy, NOT a quiet relax: the accidental-eager-load guard is init-help-cold-start (parse5 MUST stay lazy there), unaffected at ~119ms, so nothing heavy crept onto a path that should be lazy — this is the expected cold cost growing. 350 gives ~1.4x headroom over the observed 252 to absorb cross-runner variance (ubuntu-latest runners vary run-to-run), while a real eager-load regression would be 700ms+ — well clear of this cap.

validate-full-project.description: `spectastic validate "specs/**" "examples/**" inbox.html principles.html` — steady-state across the full set
validate-full-project.rationale: Scales with the corpus, now ~331 docs (was 188 when the 1600 budget was set, 34 at the original 500) — CI measures ~2233ms, a healthy ~6.75ms/doc that is still LINEAR in doc count (no O(N^2) cross-file regression, which at this count would be ~10,000ms+). The budget is ~9ms/doc (331 x ~9 = ~3000), preserving the ~1.3x CI headroom the prior budget had over its measured time: loose enough not to flake on a slow runner, tight enough to catch a real algorithmic blow-up. RAISE THIS as the spec corpus grows — a stale absolute cap is what made this fail across several merges (065 tipped 188 -> 331 past the 1600 cap); the per-doc cost is the real guard.
